questions.q: What does ls -la show that plain ls doesn't?
options: The long format (permissions, owner, size, date) plus hidden dotfiles
Only files larger than 1MB
A graphical file browser window
Nothing — the flags have no effect
questions.explain: -l switches to the long listing format and -a includes hidden files (anything starting with a dot).

questions.q: What's the real difference between mv and cp?
options: mv moves or renames a file (the original is gone); cp duplicates it (the original stays)
They are two names for the exact same command
cp only works on directories, mv only works on files
mv requires root privileges and cp never does
questions.explain: Linux treats moving and renaming as the same operation (mv), while cp leaves the original file in place and creates a copy.

questions.q: Why is less generally preferred over cat for viewing a large log file?
options: less pages through the file one screen at a time and supports searching, instead of dumping thousands of lines at once
cat cannot open files larger than 1KB
less is faster at editing file contents
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: cat prints the entire file immediately, which is unusable for a long file; less lets you page through and search with /.

questions.q: What is the real difference between what grep and find each search?
options: grep searches inside a file's content for a matching pattern; find searches the filesystem for files matching criteria like name or date
grep and find do exactly the same thing
find searches file content; grep searches the filesystem
grep only works on directories, never on files
questions.explain: grep answers "what's inside these files"; find answers "which files exist, and where."

questions.q: What does rm -r do, and why is it risky?
options: It deletes a directory and everything inside it recursively, permanently — there is no Recycle Bin on Linux
It renames a directory without deleting anything
It only marks files for deletion, recoverable later from a trash folder
It copies a directory recursively instead of deleting it
questions.explain: rm -r recursively removes a directory and its contents with no built-in undo, which is why scripts that use it are tested carefully first.
